To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the GRAPES–3 muon data are corrected for pressure variations using a new pressure measurement technique and (b) the corrected data are used to obtain the solar diurnal variation during a year of relatively low solar activities, which shows a variation in both amplitude and phase.
the solar diurnal variation measured in muons during 2006 displays significant variations in both the amplitude and phase, which may be related to solar activity.

the pressure-corrected GRAPES-2 data are used to determine the profile of the diurnal anisotropic modulation of the cosmic ray intensity during 2006 and the results show significant variation in both the amplitude (from 2% to 4%) and phase (from 0.5 to 0.9 h).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of the solar diuronal anisotropy in the cosmic ray muon flux at Ooty using GRAPES-2 experiment.
the study of the diurnal variation of the cosmic ray intensity, using muons detected at Ooty, which is situated at an altitude of 2200 m above sea level in southern India (11.4° N, 76.7° E).
the development of a novel pressure-measurement system and its use for the correction of pressure-induced variations in the GRAPES muon data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solar diurnal modulation of cosmic ray intensity, which is a well-known phenomenon, is indeed a reality.
the solar diurnal amplitude and phase are variable and depend strongly on the phase of the 11-year sunspot cycle.
the solar diurnal modulation is a complex phenomenon and its study using the GRAPES3 data will continue in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solar diurnal modulation is not only a function of solar cycle but it also depends on the solar activity during a particular solar cycle.
the solar diurnal variation in muon flux is a robust feature that can be measured with a high accuracy using the GRAPES 3 muon detector.
the pressure-corrected GRAPES- 3 muon data can be used to accurately measure the solar diurnal variations in cosmic ray intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GRAPES3 muon data are suitable for studying solar anisotropies and the pressure correction method developed here is useful for studying solar anistropies in other experiments.
the pressure-corrected GRAPES- 3 muon data can be used for detailed studies of solar modulation of cosmic rays.
, by using a large-area muon detector, one can accurately measure the profile of solar diurnal anistropy with high statistics.
